newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: ICO chief sees slight excess in 1996-97 supply.
newsitem.headline: ICO chief sees slight excess in 1996-97 supply.

text.p: Celsius Lodder, executive director of the International Coffee Organization, said he expects to see only a "slight excess in supply" during the 1996-97 coffee year and world prices ranging between $1.10 and $1.30 per lb.

Lodder, who spoke to Reuters shortly before a news conference at the National Coffee Growers Federation in Bogota, predicted coffee output of between 99 million and 100 million 60-kilo bags in the 1996-97 coffee year, which began this month and ends next September.
But he said this would be countered by demand for up to 98 million bags, including about 25 million bags that would be consumed in producer countries themselves.

"There is going to be a slight excess in supply," he said, adding however that this could hopefully be countered by growing demand for coffee in Pacific Rim countries and increasing demand for gourmet or speciality coffees in the United States.
He added that supply would be tight enough to lead to possibile volatility on world markets but predicted that prices would range no higher than about $1.30 per lb.
Demand by consumer countries will total somewhere between 72 million and 73 million 60-kilo bags in the coffee year, Lodder said. -- Juan Guillermo Londono, Bogota newsroom, 571 610 7944
